reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
ABH IL will only reimburse for polysomnography procedures when appropriately reported. 
Appropriate reporting includes 
 
Reporting an age-based procedure code that is consistent with the patients’ actual age on 
the date of service 
 
Reporting polysomnography as conducted in an appropriate place of service- not in the 
patients’ home 
 
Claims that are submitted will be denied when 
 
An age-based procedure code is reported that is inconsistent with the patients’ actual age 
on the date of service 
 
Polysomnography is reported as conducted in the patients’ home using the place of 
service code 12 
 
The medical record documentation is expected to support the specific CPT code(s) and ICD-10-
CM codes reported.

This policy outlines the coding and editing guidelines for reporting polysomnography procedures 
and applies to all professional and facility claim types. Polysomnography is a comprehensive 
diagnostic sleep study used to evaluate sleep disorders by continuously recording multiple 
physiologic parameters during sleep. These parameters typically include brain activity, eye 
movements, muscle activity, heart rhythm, respiratory effort, airflow, and oxygen saturation. 
Polysomnography is considered the standard diagnostic test for conditions such as obstructive 
sleep apnea and other sleep-related breathing disorders. 
 
When reporting polysomnography, some CPT codes require you to consider the age of the 
patient as stated in the code description. If a CPT code that references the patient’s age is 
reported, the procedure will be denied if the age range is inconsistent with the patient’s actual 
age on the date of service. 
 
Polysomnography reported as conducted in a patient’s home using the place of service code 12 
is not considered appropriate and will be denied.

Applicable CPT Codes 
95808 
Polysomnography; any age, sleep staging with 1-3 additional parameters of sleep, 
attended by a technologist 
95810 
Polysomnography; age 6 years or older, sleep staging with 4 or more additional 
parameters of sleep, attended by a technologist 
95811 
Polysomnography; age 6 years or older, sleep staging with 4 or more additional 
parameters of sleep, with initiation of continuous positive airway pressure therapy or 
bilevel ventilation, attended by a technologist 
95782 
Polysomnography; younger than 6 years, sleep staging with 4 or more additional 
parameters of sleep, attended by a technologist 
 
95783 
Polysomnography; younger than 6 years, sleep staging with 4 or more additional 
parameters of sleep, with initiation of continuous positive airway pressure therapy or 
bi-level ventilation, attended by a technologist
